title: Jensen Huang's Fall Hits 'Open' Models In Boost to Anthropic and OpenAI - Slashdot
excerpt: Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia could weaken the open AI model ecosystem he spent years championing, potentially strengthening closed-model developers like OpenAI and Anthropic, according to the Financial Times. content_html:
Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia could weaken the open AI model ecosystem he spent years championing, potentially strengthening closed-model developers like OpenAI and Anthropic, according to the Financial Times. From the report: The US chip giant's former chief threw Nvidia's balance sheet into creating a broad AI ecosystem, including by seeding and acquiring start-ups involved in the development of open-source and open-weight models, which users can customize and run on their own hardware. Huang was a forceful advocate for their spread, lobbying against Washington's moves to restrict the use of Chinese-made open models while seeking the development of US alternatives. "Our AI leadership will be judged not by one frontier AI model, but by whether the United States builds a strong, open ecosystem that diffuses into every sector," he wrote this summer in his first-ever message on X.

His ignominious exit from Nvidia deprives the open model sector of its most vocal and influential supporter in the US. "I think Jensen stood to gain the most economically and was personally committed to diversity at the model layer," said one venture capitalist who has invested in AI start-ups alongside Nvidia. "Without him and a less generous Nvidia in terms of investment, we may end up in a much more concentrated world of model providers."

Whether Nvidia will continue the rapid pace of dealmaking under a new leader is unclear. The company was expected to participate in or lead four start-up deals currently under discussion: investments in Thinking Machines Lab and Groq, a potential partnership with Reflection AI and the $12.9bn acquisition of open model repository Hugging Face.

"Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia, but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," said Elon Musk in a post on X on Saturday. "Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost."

"In some sense [Huang leaving Nvidia] is bad for the industry, but in some sense Jensen is an enemy of the frontier labs because he wants models to become commoditized so he retains the prime position in the value chain," said one senior figure at a leading Silicon Valley AI company.

"I don't think open weight models are going away... but losing Jensen as their greatest financial backer and champion will slow their progress, and I imagine will not hurt Anthropic's IPO," said another industry figure.

"It's reasonable to expect the ouster of Jensen will concentrate computing power more in the hands of frontier labs and hyperscalers," added a senior figure at an AI lab. "That's good for the labs."
